items.followUp: Mention two precautions that help protect a computer user from phishing.

rubric.why: Avoiding suspicious links and messages, and checking who sent them, can help prevent phishing.
rubric.description: Avoid suspicious links or messages, or verify the sender.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for advising the user to avoid suspicious links or emails, or to verify the sender before responding.

rubric.why: Phishing attempts commonly try to obtain passwords and other private information.
rubric.description: Do not share passwords or other sensitive information through untrusted messages or websites.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for advising against sharing passwords or sensitive information through an untrusted source.

modelAnswer: Do not open links or attachments in suspicious emails or messages; verify the sender before responding.
Never share passwords or other sensitive information through an untrusted website or message.

items.followUp: How many bits are in an IPv6 address, and how is it usually written?

rubric.why: An IPv6 address has a length of 128 bits.
rubric.description: State the length of an IPv6 address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an IPv6 address is 128 bits long.

rubric.why: IPv6 addresses are commonly represented as colon-separated groups of hexadecimal digits.
rubric.description: Describe the usual written form of an IPv6 address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is written in hexadecimal groups separated by colons.

modelAnswer: An IPv6 address is a 128-bit address.
It is usually written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits separated by colons.
